title: Runtime mapping safeguards and version pin exemptions for open models
creator: Sana Patel
description: Clarify and formalize the runtime compatibility mapping and the exception workflow for version pinning when onboarding community/open models into the Redwood model catalog. Goal: reduce two classes of production incidents — (1) model variant mismatches that surface as runtime failures (kernel/quantization/kv-cache mismatches), and (2) silent regressions when an unpinned upstream model changes behavior. Deliver a minimal spec, acceptance tests, console metadata fields, and an operator playbook for pin exemptions.
background: We regularly accept community-provided weights and variants. Recent incidents showed gaps: some variants require different kernel selection or KV cache layout (sequence-length and layernorm differences) which we only catch in production, and other times maintainers push non-semantic changes upstream that cause behavior drift because we accepted unpinned variants. Current intake is informal and creates operational toil for runtime and platform teams.
scope: In scope: define runtime-compat metadata fields required at intake, a small set of compatibility tiers (Strict/Fallback/Experimental), automated pre-merge runtime smoke tests for each tier, console UI labels and tooltips, and an operator workflow for requesting pin-exemptions with risk approvals. Out of scope: full semver enforcement for every upstream model and retrofitting all existing catalog entries in this ticket.
out_of_scope: Full retroactive pinning for entire catalog, deep model fidelity evaluation (separate eval project), and changes to upstream community licensing policies.
requirements: Add three runtime compatibility tiers: strict, fallback, experimental. Document exact guarantees for each tier.
Require 'runtime_signature' metadata on intake describing expected kernel/quantization/memory layout attributes as a free-text + structured tag (string list).
Console: Display 'compatibility_tier' and 'runtime_signature' on model details page and in onboarding checklist.

On intake: run automated runtime smoke tests on the target Dedicated/Hosted runtime variants declared by the contributor. Smoke tests must include: load & forward pass with representative sequence lengths, KV cache warm-start test, and quantized vs float forward comparison tolerance check.
If smoke tests fail for 'strict' tier, onboarding must be blocked. For 'fallback' tier, onboarding allowed but UI must show explicit fallback mapping and auto-routing policy must be configured.
Define a documented 'pin-exemption' request flow: author must provide justification, risk assessment, and agree to quarterly checkpointing; exemption requires sign-off from Runtime Lead and PM.
Add an automated alerting rule to surface downstream model drift if model outputs change beyond threshold across two consecutive daily eval runs (integration with Optimize).
Add acceptance tests to CI that validate metadata presence and that the runtime smoke-suite passes in the intake pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: PRD reviewed and approved by Runtime, Platform, and Developer Experience leads.
A minimal runtime_compatibility schema (json-schema as doc artifact) is created and linked from intake flow.

Intake pipeline (staging) runs the runtime smoke-suite against declared runtime variants and enforces blocking behavior for 'strict' tier. Link to test run: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-intake/actions/runs/398127
Console UI shows compatibility tier and runtime_signature on model pages; onboarding checklist requires these fields to proceed.
Operator playbook for pin-exemptions written and approved; includes template justification, signer list, and rollback criteria.

Two representative community model onboardings completed in staging using the new flow (one 'fallback', one 'experimental') and documented in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/MOD/Runtime+Compatibility+Intake
E2E alerting rule in Optimize created to detect drift and wired to #model-catalog-ops Slack channel with playbook link.
dependencies: ENG-4210 (intake pipeline changes for CI integration)
ENG-4389 (smoke-suite test harness and quantization comparator)
deliverables: Runtime compatibility spec doc (runtime_compatibility_schema_v1.md) with examples and allowed tags.
Updated intake pipeline that runs smoke-suite and enforces tier blocking rules.
Console UI updates to render compatibility metadata and pin-exemption status.
Operator playbook and pin-exemption request template in Confluence.
CI acceptance tests for metadata presence and smoke-suite execution.
notes: Trade-offs discussed on 2025-09-22: strict tier adds onboarding friction but prevents production outages; fallback tier is operationally cheaper but requires clear UI and automated routing policies.
Runtime Lead (Anika Bose) advocated for limiting exemptions to <10% of intake population and requiring quarterly checkpoints.
Proposal to include a machine-readable 'kernel_hint' tag (e.g., 'fused-attn:flash', 'matmul-cuBLAS:default') to help runtime select optimized kernels; exact tag set TBD with ENG-4389.
We will pilot with two community models: 'mosaic-13B-quant' (fallback) and 'open-dialogue-xl' (experimental).
Security review flagged that pin-exempt models may need additional audit logging; ENG to add flag for audit export. Refer to security ticket ENG-4521.
